notes_for_editor: Thin primary evidence: the corpus (Marine branch reports from 1900) has nothing on Newfoundland, which was not part of Canada until 1949, so the story rests on Parks Canada, the Canadian Register of Historic Places and Lighthouse Friends (a secondary source, kept to paraphrase). Conflicts left stated in the text: built 1835 vs lit 1836; fog horn 1877 (LHF) vs 1878 (Parks Canada); Gerry Cantwell keeper from 1969 (Parks caption) vs head keeper from 1982 (LHF); James Cantwell died 1880 vs Sheppard/LHF dates. The Prince Henry anecdote is LHF only. Roster is LHF's list, not a primary register; Michael Cantwell has no years. Journal of the House of Assembly of Newfoundland and Molloy's The First Landfall would improve it. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Register 20775 dates the new lighthouse to 1953, others 1955 (stated in text). Gerry/Gerald and Parks 1969 caption linked by first name only because LHF's own narrative calls him Gerry; flagged in text.
